image.alt: Fronius Wattpilot Flex Home 11 C6; maker range photo showing the shared Flex Home housing.

pros: Uses spare solar power, adjusting charging as sunshine changes.
Touch buttons and a charging display let you check and change settings on the unit.
The fixed 6-metre cable is included, without needing a separate charging lead.
cons: On single-phase power, this 11 kW model is limited to 3.68 kW.
Solar charging needs a Fronius meter; third-party solar may also need extra control equipment.
Cannot send the car's stored energy back into your home.

chargingPower.basis: Published maximum 11 kW AC output on three-phase power; single-phase maximum is 3.68 kW. The car and configured supply limits set actual output.

warranty.basis: Current AU maker FAQ gives three years for the charger product from August 2024. Separate meters, controls and installation are outside this selected charger unit.

technicalSpecs.label: Maximum charging power

technicalSpecs.label: Included cable
technicalSpecs.value: 6 m attached cable with a Type 2 car plug.

technicalSpecs.label: Solar charging range
technicalSpecs.value: Adjusts spare-solar charging from 1.38 to 11 kW under the published supply conditions.

technicalSpecs.label: Solar equipment
technicalSpecs.value: Requires a Fronius Smart Meter; third-party solar needs Smart Meter IP or a Datamanager Box 2.0 with a Smart Meter.

technicalSpecs.label: Controls and connections
technicalSpecs.value: On-unit touch buttons and charging display; Solar.wattpilot app, WiFi and wired Ethernet.

technicalSpecs.label: Outdoor use
technicalSpecs.value: IP66; installs upright indoors or outdoors.

technicalSpecs.label: Size and weight
technicalSpecs.value: 325 x 195 x 105 mm; 4.1 kg including the cable.

technicalSpecs.label: Operating temperature
technicalSpecs.value: -25 to +45 degrees Celsius.

technicalSpecs.label: Parts warranty
technicalSpecs.value: Three-year charger product warranty under the current Australian maker FAQ.

technicalSpecs.label: Car-to-home power
technicalSpecs.value: Does not currently support sending car battery energy into the home or grid.

freshness.note: The Flex generation was announced in November 2024 ahead of market launch and appears in 2025 maker training. The January 2026 AU sheet identifies this exact version; the first AU launch day is not established.
